points.minimum: The answer must cover each of these core website disclosures. (a) Daily portfolio holdings, posted before the opening of regular trading on the primary listing exchange. These are the holdings that form the basis for the next NAV calculation (prior-close/T+1 holdings), not the creation/redemption basket. Each holding must show an identifier such as ticker or CUSIP, a description, the quantity (shares or par/notional), and its percentage weight. (b) The prior business day's NAV, market price (closing price or midpoint of the bid/ask at NAV calculation time) and the resulting premium/discount. (c) A historical premium/discount presentation, as a table and/or line graph. (d) The 30-day median bid-ask spread. (e) The sustained-deviation trigger: a premium or discount above 2% for more than seven consecutive trading days requires a website statement of that fact plus a discussion of the factors reasonably believed to have contributed to it. Optional subdetails: the statement is posted on the trading day after the seventh consecutive day; the market price may be the closing price or the bid/ask midpoint; citation to Rule 6c-11(c)(1)-(2). Half credit if (a) and (b) are correct but (c), (d) or (e) is missing or materially incomplete. Half credit if (e) is stated without the >2% / >7-consecutive-trading-day thresholds.

Technical detail, credited as enrichment only. The historical table shows the number of days the shares traded at a premium and at a discount, typically with a line graph of daily premiums/discounts. The median spread is computed from NBBO observations taken every 10 seconds during regular trading hours on each trading day in the last 30 calendar days. Each spread is divided by the NBBO midpoint, the median is taken, and the result is expressed as a percentage rounded to the nearest hundredth. Retention of the sustained-deviation statement for at least one year is also credited here or under point 1. If the answer gives 30 trading days instead of 30 calendar days, or an incorrect sampling basis, deduct only when stated as fact; this is not central unless it contradicts point 1(d) entirely.

The answer must state that the premium/discount history covers the most recently completed calendar year plus any calendar quarters completed since then. If the fund has existed for less time, the history covers its life. The answer must also state that the website disclosures must be publicly available and free of charge, with no paywall, registration or subscription. Half credit if only one of these two elements (history period or public/free) is present.

central_errors: Stating that portfolio holdings need only be disclosed periodically (e.g., monthly, quarterly, or with a lag) rather than daily before market open.

Equating or substituting the creation/redemption (transaction) basket for the portfolio holdings disclosure, e.g., claiming that publishing the basket satisfies the holdings requirement or that the website holdings must reflect the basket. Rule 6c-11 requires full portfolio holdings on the website; basket composition is governed by internal basket policies and recordkeeping and is not the holdings disclosure.

Giving the wrong sustained-deviation trigger as a definitive rule, e.g., a 1% threshold, any single day, or 'seven days' framed as calendar days or as 'at least seven' instead of more than seven consecutive trading days above 2%.
Stating that the sustained-deviation statement may be removed once the deviation ends, or that it is filed only with the SEC rather than posted on the website.

Stating that the premium/discount history must cover a materially different required period, e.g., only the prior day or a fixed five years, instead of the last calendar year plus completed quarters (or fund life).
Stating that the website disclosures may be behind a paywall, registration or subscription.
Stating that ETFs relying on Rule 6c-11 need not disclose a median bid-ask spread, or that the spread is a quarterly average from Form N-1A rather than a 30-day median posted on the website.

scoring_rule.correct: Fully satisfies the minimums for both required points (1 and 3) and contains no central error. This includes daily pre-open holdings with identifier, description, quantity and weight; prior-day NAV, market price and premium/discount; historical table/graph; 30-day median spread; the >2%/>7-consecutive-trading-day statement with a contributing-factors discussion; the last-calendar-year-plus-completed-quarters history (or fund life); and public, free access. The answer also distinguishes portfolio holdings from transaction baskets, at least implicitly by not conflating them. Point 2 detail is not needed for full credit.
scoring_rule.partial: No central error, but one or more required minimums are only partly met, using the half-credit rules defined per point. Examples: omitting the history period or the public/free requirement; omitting the spread or the historical presentation; describing the sustained-deviation explanation without the thresholds. Also partial: an answer that states the holdings disclosure correctly but does not explicitly address the holdings-versus-basket distinction. Score is the sum of earned weights, with point 1 weighted about 2/3 and point 3 about 1/3. Partial if the total is between roughly 40% and 90%.
scoring_rule.wrong: Contains any central error stated as fact. Also wrong: an answer missing the daily holdings disclosure entirely, or covering under about 40% of the required content. Omissions alone, including the point 2 technical detail, do not make an answer wrong.
